Subject: Question: EU pin confirmation + temporary egress window for backups

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency graphs. Legal and procurement have two blocking asks before we can close:

1) A firm commitment that customer-designated EU data can be pinned to EU-hosted execution and telemetry for the primary workload (we understand there may be transient syncs for caches). We need description of the failure-mode/egress behavior and max window for non-EU processing.

2) Subprocessor roster and a DPA addendum template that covers the transient egress scenario (how long, what triggers it, logging/audit evidence). Procurement wants to understand whether this will require a bespoke annex or an approved Redwood addendum we can sign via DocuSign.

Can you confirm next steps and timeline? Ideally we need procurement sign-off in the next two weeks.

Thanks,
Alice

Subject: Re: Question: EU pin confirmation + temporary egress window for backups

Hi Alice / team — looping in Legal. Attached: DPA_Addendum_MedTech_v1.pdf (redline-friendly) and Subprocessor_Roster_Q3.csv. Key points from the draft addendum:

- Scope: Customer-designated EU data will be routed to EU execution endpoints. Redwood will maintain primary processing and telemetry within EU regions by default.
- Transient egress: defined as temporary processing outside EU for maintenance, capacity overflow, or disaster recovery. Max per-event window: 72 hours, cumulative maximum 168 hours per 12-month rolling period unless mutually agreed.
- Notification & approvals: Redwood will notify the named DPO and provide a summary of trigger reason, timestamps, systems affected, and audit logs within 24 hours of the transient event end.
- Audit evidence: we will provide an anonymized audit log extract and a connection/egress heatmap (redacted) from the time window.
- KMS & keys: By default customer data encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed keys. Customer-managed CMKs available as an add-on; language included.
- Subprocessor limits: list attached; any changes to EU-resident critical subprocessors will be communicated 30 days prior with options for escrow/acceptable substitute.

This is intentionally conservative — we can tighten windows or add additional telemetry obligations if MedTech needs. If procurement prefers, we can implement the addendum as either: 1) an annex to the standard Redwood DPA, or 2) a short SOW addendum that references the DPA. Both routes support DocuSign execution.

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_MedTech_v1.pdf (draft addendum, redline encouraged), Subprocessor_Roster_Q3.csv, TransientEgress_Runbook.odt (ops runbook sketch).

If this looks acceptable in principle, please indicate the preferred execution path (Annex vs SOW) and procurement lead; I will prepare a DocuSign-ready package.

-Karthik

Thanks Karthik — Procurement reviewed the proposed windows and the notification commitments. Two quick asks before we route to approval:

- Can you shorten the per-event window to 48 hours (still accept cumulative 168 hours annual)? MedTech's policy prefers smaller single-event windows, but we can be flexible if there are compelling operational constraints.
- Please include a single paragraph that states the addendum is not a substitute for a security review; we will still perform a brief vendor security checklist but signing the addendum will be the gating procurement action.

If you can update the DPA addendum with a 48-hour event max and the procurement paragraph, we will circulate internally and aim to sign within 5 business days. Also confirm you will provide the DocuSign package and a HubSpot deal reference so our systems can pick it up.
